prompts.title: Precision Customer Email

prompts.content: Write a persuasive outreach email to [AUDIENCE] regarding [TOPIC]. Tone: [TONE]. Strict constraints: Under 120 words, no marketing buzzwords, compelling value proposition, and a single friction-free call to action.

prompts.title: Minimalist Studio Product Still Life

prompts.content: One [SUBJECT] placed precisely in the center of a seamless neutral matte studio surface. Soft continuous diffused lighting from the upper left, gentle realistic contact shadows. Strict exclusions: no text, no branding, no secondary objects, no patterned background.

prompts.title: Clean Isometric 3D Asset
prompts.description: Smooth 3D icon or asset with balanced ambient occlusion.
prompts.content: Clean isometric 3D render of [SUBJECT]. Vibrant minimalist color palette, matte clay shader with soft ambient occlusion, isolated on a uniform dark background. No floating particles or distracting glare.

prompts.title: Production API Endpoint with Validation

prompts.content: Implement a production-grade API endpoint in [LANGUAGE] using [FRAMEWORK] that handles [FEATURE]. Strictly include input validation, proper HTTP status codes, structured error handling, and complete type definitions. Do not include unnecessary boilerplate.

prompts.title: Accessible Interactive UI Component

prompts.content: Build a fully accessible, reusable [COMPONENT] in [LANGUAGE] using [FRAMEWORK]. Requirements: Complete keyboard accessibility (Tab, Enter, Escape, Arrow keys), ARIA labels, clear state management, and responsive styling. Return only the component code.

prompts.title: High-Performance Data Transformation

prompts.content: Write an optimized utility function in [LANGUAGE] to process [DATA_TYPE] data. Must handle nullish values, empty collections, and malformed inputs gracefully. Optimal time and space complexity, fully typed with unit test examples.

generations.prompt: Write a TypeScript function to debounce another function with cancellation support.
Give exactly 3 bullet points defining idempotency in REST APIs.
generations.output:
* **State Consistency:** An HTTP request is idempotent if executing it multiple identical times produces the exact same server-side resource state as executing it once.
* **Method Classification:** Standard HTTP methods like GET, HEAD, PUT, and DELETE are designed to be idempotent, whereas POST is non-idempotent because repeated calls typically create multiple distinct resources.
* **Server State vs. Response:** Idempotency guarantees the side effects on the server remain identical, not that the returned HTTP status code or response body will be the same (e.g., an initial DELETE returning 200/204 while subsequent calls return 404).
